summary.name: Taming chaos: Preparing for your next incident
summary.one_liner: An O'Reilly interview with Google SREs Tim Craig and Gustavo Franco on building organization-wide incident response processes, training, and management buy-in.
use_cases: Planning an incident response program for an engineering organization
Deciding which incident types to train staff on
Getting management approval for incident response training
Learning how Google approaches incident handling
summary.what_it_does: The article is an interview with Google SREs Tim Craig and Gustavo Franco about incident response. It argues that incident response is an organizational issue that spans many teams, not only SREs and network administrators, and that processes matter more than tools. It recommends regular training, choosing incident types that teach staff well, and starting small with simple notes-on-paper reviews of how incidents are handled. It also covers automating disaster recovery tests to lower cost and effort and to win management approval. The page defines MTTM (median time to mitigate) and SLO terms and points to the incident response chapter of The Site Reliability Workbook.
notable: Interview format with two Google engineers on organization-wide incident response
Emphasizes processes and people over tools, with training analogous to CPR refreshers
Points to the incident response chapter of The Site Reliability Workbook for more detail
caveats: Article is a discussion piece, not a tool; it gives no step-by-step procedures or software to install
Describes Google's practices, which the author notes took 15 years to develop and may be far larger than most teams need
